Headquarters: United States - Remote

Tebra only initiates contact with candidates via email from an official Tebra email address (@tebra.com, @patientpop.com, or @kareo.com) or through our applicant tracking system, Greenhouse. We will only ask you to provide sensitive personal information through our official application portal — not via social media or text message. We do not conduct interviews via instant messaging.
About the Role

We’re looking for a Manager of GTM Engineering to help build the data and activation engine behind Tebra’s next generation of outbound growth. You’ll help create and evolve a comprehensive Total Addressable Market database of independent healthcare practices and related businesses, combining public, proprietary, and third-party data into actionable segments, signals, and outbound workflows. This role sits at the intersection of data engineering, Clay, GTM systems, and outbound strategy—and is ideal for someone who can both architect the system and get hands-on building the workflows that turn market intelligence into a pipeline.

Your Area of Focus

• Build and evolve Tebra’s TAM database, creating a reliable and actionable view of independent healthcare practices, providers, billing companies, and other priority market segments.

• Own sophisticated Clay workflows and architecture, including enrichment waterfalls, provider and vendor integrations, scoring logic, custom signals, AI research, segmentation, and activation.

• Integrate data from multiple sources, including public datasets, APIs, enrichment vendors, web scraping, internal systems, and proprietary data, into a scalable GTM data model.

• Manage and develop two GTM Engineers, spanning database infrastructure and Clay/AI automation; translate business priorities into a clear technical roadmap, allocate work across the team, remove blockers, and ensure solutions are scalable, reliable, and tied to measurable GTM outcomes.

• Design and maintain the connection between Clay, Snowflake, Salesforce, Outreach, and other GTM systems, ensuring data can move reliably from source to enrichment to segmentation to activation.

• Build data quality and governance mechanisms, including deduplication, validation, suppression logic, enrichment freshness, field mapping, monitoring, and auditability.

• Develop and operationalize market signals that improve how we identify, prioritize, and engage prospective customers, including firmographic, technographic, behavioral, competitive, and other trigger-based signals.

• Partner with Marketing program owners and Sales leaders to co-develop outbound strategy, translating ICP, campaign, and market hypotheses into executable targeting, enrichment, and activation workflows.

• Design and test outbound motions that use improved data, AI, personalization, and trigger-based targeting to increase relevance and conversion while maintaining appropriate unit economics.

• Own the technical architecture behind outbound experimentation, enabling the organization to quickly test new audiences, signals, channels, personalization strategies, and campaign concepts.

• Monitor the economics of the GTM data stack, including enrichment usage, API costs, Clay credits, vendor overlap, cost per enriched record, and other infrastructure costs.

• Build monitoring and alerting for data pipeline failures, enrichment gaps, sync issues, activation problems, and other conditions that could impact outbound performance.

• Create scalable systems rather than one-off lists, designing architecture, documentation, and governance that allow Tebra’s TAM data and outbound capabilities to compound over time.

Your Professional Qualifications

• 5+ years of relevant experience across GTM engineering, growth engineering, data engineering, revenue operations, outbound systems, technical growth, or a related discipline.

• Deep, hands-on experience with Clay, including building production-scale workflows, enrichment waterfalls, APIs, custom logic, scoring, AI enrichment, and downstream activation.

• Strong proficiency with SQL, APIs, webhooks, and scripting using Python, JavaScript, or similar languages.

• Experience working with cloud data warehouses such as Snowflake and understanding data modeling, ingestion, transformation, and data quality concepts.

• Experience integrating and operationalizing large or complex datasets from sources such as public registries, enrichment providers, scraping platforms, and third-party APIs.

• Experience with GTM systems such as Salesforce, Outreach, ZoomInfo, Marketo, Slack, and related enrichment or activation tools.

• Strong understanding of modern outbound strategy, including segmentation, ICP development, account prioritization, enrichment, trigger-based outbound, personalization, and campaign measurement.

• Experience building or supporting web scraping and external data collection workflows using tools such as Apify, SerpAPI, browser automation, or similar technologies.

• Strong understanding of data quality, deduplication, matching, governance, monitoring, and maintaining production-grade data systems.

• Ability to think in systems and unit economics, balancing technical sophistication with cost, reliability, speed, and commercial value.

• Strong analytical and commercial judgment, with the ability to connect data architecture and technical decisions to pipeline creation and revenue outcomes.

• Ability to work closely with Marketing, Sales, Analytics, and technical teams and translate between GTM strategy and implementation.

• Experience in B2B SaaS, SMB go-to-market motions, healthcare, healthcare data, or provider data is preferred but not required.

Headquarters: Remote, USA

Help empower our global customers to connect to culture through their passions.
Why you’ll love this role:

StockX has redefined the global marketplace for culture — where buyers and sellers transact with confidence on an always-on digital exchange. We are building the next frontier of creator-driven, culturally rich commerce that blends excitement, community, expertise, and transaction in one platform.

To power this next chapter, we are building a category-led organization where each major vertical operates with clear ownership, accountability, and cultural authority.

The Director, Category Growth (General Manager) is the business owner of a major category vertical. This leader is accountable for the full P&L and long-term trajectory of their category — including supply growth, liquidity, demand activation, monetization, and marketplace health.

You will operate as a true GM: setting vision, defining strategy, allocating resources, building a team, and driving cross-functional execution. You will represent your vertical at the leadership level and ensure that product, marketing, operations, and partnerships are aligned to unlock sustainable growth.

This role is both entrepreneurial and executive — suited for a leader who wants to build and scale a culturally driven business within a high-impact marketplace.

What you’ll own:

Full-Stack Category P&L

• Own revenue, contribution margin, liquidity, and growth targets for your vertical

• Develop annual and multi-year business plans, forecasts, and investment cases

• Allocate resources across acquisition, retention, and engagement to maximize ROI

• Drive pricing, incentives, and promotional strategies aligned to marketplace health

Vertical Strategy & Market Leadership

• Define the long-term category vision, positioning, and competitive differentiation

• Identify expansion opportunities across adjacent segments, geographies, and seller tiers

• Establish scalable supply acquisition and retention strategies

• Continuously assess competitive dynamics and evolving cultural trends

Supply, Demand & Liquidity Engine

• Architect the playbook for acquiring, activating, and retaining high-value sellers and creators

• Ensure balanced marketplace dynamics between supply depth and demand velocity

• Partner with Growth and Marketing to stimulate demand moments and category engagement

• Implement structural improvements that increase conversion, retention, and monetization

Cross-Functional Executive Leadership

• Influence Product roadmap to improve seller tooling, pricing mechanics, discovery, and trust features

• Partner with Marketing to launch culturally relevant campaigns and high-impact moments

• Collaborate with Operations to optimize onboarding, seller support, and fulfillment performance

• Represent your vertical in executive planning, QBRs, and strategic reviews

Team & Organizational Build-Out

• Hire and develop Category Managers and supporting roles as the vertical scales

• Establish operating cadence, reporting frameworks, and performance management systems

• Build repeatable GTM playbooks that can be deployed across additional categories

• Foster a culture of accountability, experimentation, and community authenticity

Ecosystem & Community Stewardship

• Act as the senior face of StockX within your category’s ecosystem

• Build relationships with top sellers, shops, creators, and community leaders

• Ensure platform growth remains culturally credible and aligned with community norms

About you:

• 10+ years of experience in marketplace leadership, category general management, business development, or growth roles within consumer tech or two-sided platforms

• Demonstrated ownership of revenue or P&L-level outcomes

• Proven track record of scaling a vertical, marketplace segment, or new business line

• Strong executive presence and experience influencing cross-functional roadmaps

• Deep fluency in marketplace mechanics: liquidity, take rate, CAC/LTV, cohort behavior, supply elasticity

• Experienced people leader with a track record of building high-performing teams

• Deep connection to culture-driven or enthusiast categories

Why this role is different: 

This is not a traditional category marketing or merchandising role. This is a vertical GM role with real business ownership.

You will:

• Build and scale a culturally driven marketplace vertical from early-stage to maturity

About Gusto

At Gusto, we're on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. With teams in Denver, San Francisco, and New York, we support more than 500,000 small businesses nationwide and are building a workplace that reflects the people we serve.

All full-time employees receive competitive base pay, benefits, and equity (RSUs) — because everyone who helps build Gusto should share in its success. Offer amounts are determined by role, level, and location. Learn more about our Total Rewards philosophy.

AI is a fundamental part of how work gets done at Gusto. We expect all team members to actively engage with AI tools relevant to their role and grow their fluency as the technology evolves. AI experience requirements vary by role and will be assessed during the interview process.
About Design at Gusto: 

Design at Gusto is made up of over 80 creative, collaborative people who care deeply about our mission to empower small businesses and their employees. We're a cross-functional group that is always looking for opportunities to build understanding and empathy for the people who use Gusto. We don't care much about swim lanes and though we care deeply about quality and craft, we are never precious about it. We work closely with cross-functional partners in Product, Engineering, Data, and Marketing to design, build, and ship experiences that make a real difference. We believe great design can make hard things possible, even delightful.

We are building an AI-native design organization — and we mean that seriously. We're looking for designers who are already working this way: using AI to prototype ideas quickly, shorten customer feedback loops, and ship quality UX directly to customers. This isn't a future aspiration — it's how we work now, and it's changing what the design role looks like at Gusto and across the industry.

About the Role:

For the hundreds of thousands of small businesses we serve, our mission starts with one of their most critical responsibilities: paying their team. Getting payroll right isn’t just a feature—it’s the foundation of trust with every business that relies on us.

As the Product Design Manager for Payroll, you'll lead design in this senior level position for one of Gusto's most complex and consequential product areas, shaping the future of a product that millions of people rely on for financial stability and personal prosperity. This is a high-impact, high-visibility role with broad scope. You'll manage a team of designers and set the UX direction for Payroll, partnering closely with Product, Engineering, Research, Data, Ops, Compliance, and others to take on payroll complexity so our customers don't have to.

Your work will include simplifying complex, reciprocal workflows, defining a long-term UX vision and rallying others around it, and leading automation and AI initiatives that make the work of paying a team disappear. You'll also mentor designers, set the quality and judgment standard for AI-assisted design work across the broader Design team, and contribute to platform standards that help others across Gusto build consistent, high-quality experiences.

About the Team:

Payroll is the foundation of Gusto and our most-used, most-loved product. It’s the first Gusto experience many customers interact with, and it continues to power their success as they grow. Payroll also underpins our broader ecosystem, enabling the adoption of Benefits, Time Tracking, HR tools, and so much more. Our team is tasked with evolving and scaling this core experience for small businesses of all sizes, from solo entrepreneurs to growing companies. We focus on taking on the complexity of payroll so our customers don’t have to—making payroll faster, more flexible, and increasingly hands off.

Here’s what you’ll do day-to-day:

• 

Lead end-to-end design for Payroll — shaping experiences that help small businesses pay their teams correctly, on time, and with confidence.

• 

Define and communicate the long-term UX vision for Payroll, and rally multiple teams around it.

• 

Partner with Product, Engineering, Data, Ops and others to set strategy and roadmaps.

• 

Lead product initiatives where AI and automation are central to the user experience, simplifying payroll and reducing manual work without compromising accuracy or trust.

• 

Collaborate with Research and Data to uncover customer insights and translate them into clear, actionable UX priorities.

• 

Influence product and technical roadmaps by advocating for design quality, customer needs, and long-term system health.

• 

Set the quality and judgment standard for all design work — whether AI-assisted or not — including when to push further and when outputs meet the bar.

• 

Define and scale shared patterns, principles, and standards that promote quality, consistency, and velocity.

• 

Manage and grow a team of designers, providing mentorship, clear direction, and hands-on support across the team.

• 

Champion the Payroll experience as the foundation of Gusto's broader People Platform, ensuring seamless integration across Benefits, Time & Attendance, and third-party tools.

Here’s what we're looking for:

• 

8–10+ years of product design experience, with at least 3 years leading and managing design teams.

• 

Experience designing in complex domains i.e. financial products, healthcare, or similarly regulated environments.

• 

Experience setting UX direction across multiple teams and influencing product strategy — not just executing on it.

• 

Proven ability to drive alignment across cross-functional partners and represent design in high-stakes, strategic conversations.

• 

Deep systems thinking, with a track record of turning interconnected, complex workflows into experiences that feel simple and intuitive.

• 

Clear, direct communication and storytelling skills, with the ability to explain design decisions and influence partners at all levels.

• 

A genuine bond to Gusto's mission and the needs of small businesses.

Ideally you have:

• Demonstrated ability to assess AI-generated design directions: knowing when to use them, when to override them, and how to raise the quality bar on AI outputs.

• Experience leading product initiatives where AI or automation is central to the user experience — including how to represent uncertainty, surface errors gracefully, and preserve user agency when automation gets it wrong, particularly in high-stakes contexts.

• Experience leading a team through an AI workflow transition — not just adopting AI personally, but changing how a team works, including establishing new norms and standards.

At Gusto, we strive to provide rewards that empower employees to achieve their financial and personal goals. We offer competitive compensation packages with a strong emphasis on equity based compensation (ownership in Gusto). To learn more about Gusto’s compensation philosophy and benefits offerings please view our Total Rewards Approach page.

Headquarters: U.S. Remote

About Flexport: 

At Flexport, we believe global trade can move the human race forward. That’s why it’s our mission to make global commerce so easy there will be more of it. We’re shaping the future of a $10T industry with solutions powered by innovative technology and exceptional people. Today, companies of all sizes—from emerging brands to Fortune 500s—use Flexport technology to move more than $19B of merchandise across 112 countries a year. 

The recent global supply chain crisis has put Flexport center stage as we continue to play a pivotal role in how goods move around the world. We are proud to have the support of the best investors in the game who believe in our mission, solutions and people. Ready to tackle global challenges that impact business, society, and the environment? Come join us.
What you'll do

There is no MSSP and no tier-1 queue here. Detection & Response engineers own their detections end to end: you write them, you tune them, and your team is paged when they fire. The security team is spread across the globe with a follow-the-sun pager rotation so nobody is paged at 3am local.

The adversaries are real. The business is growing fast and the threat surface is growing with it. Defining the necessary telemetry is part of the job.

Detection engineering

• Build and tune detections across endpoint, identity, SaaS, and cloud, treating them as software: version-controlled, peer-reviewed, and shipped through the same CI/CD practices the rest of engineering uses.

• Track detection quality as measured quantities: coverage against MITRE ATT&CK, precision, time-to-detect. We don’t build-and-forget here.

Response & automation

• Own incident response: triage, contain, remediate, and write the retrospective that turns the incident into a systemic fix.

• Build automation that removes toil from investigations, and partner closely with the US-based team so context carries across time zones instead of getting lost at handoff.

Telemetry & partnership

• Define telemetry requirements for new systems before they ship, working with infrastructure and product teams to close visibility gaps rather than discovering them during an incident.

• Threat hunt proactively across the estate, converting hypotheses into either new detections or documented coverage.

You Should Have

• Typically 5–8 years of experience in detection engineering, incident response, or threat hunting, with real hands-on time writing and tuning detections. We care more about what you've built than the exact number.

• Proficiency in at least one programming language (Python, Go, or similar) and comfort writing production-grade detection and automation code.

• Experience with a modern SIEM or detection pipeline (Panther, Elastic, Splunk, or similar). What matters is that you've shipped and tuned detection logic in production.

• Practical incident response experience: you've led or played a major role in triaging and closing out real security incidents.

Nice to have

• Experience treating detections as code with CI/CD, peer review, and staged rollout.

• Experience defining telemetry contracts for systems before they ship, rather than retrofitting logging after an incident.

• A track record of critically evaluating and verifying AI-assisted work - testing, source-checking, validation - rather than trusting agent output by default. If you haven’t already spotted the em dashes in this job description and already thought about where the hiring manager (hi!) has put hands on keyboard and compared that to where they let the LLM watermarks through, you might not be the right person for the job.

• Familiarity with cloud-native and Kubernetes telemetry.

• Experience with fraud or financial-crime detection patterns.

How we work

• We stay closely aligned with teammates on other continents via Slack, video, and async docs.

• We have the latest hardware and software, including frontier AI models on day one.

• We're agile, but not dogmatic. Teams decide how they work best.

Why this role is special

• You own your detections end to end, no MSSP, no tier-1 queue, no handing your work to someone else to triage.

• The consequences here are physical, not abstract: a containment decision can stop a customs filing or freight actually moving, which makes the stakes concrete in a way a SaaS control plane rarely is.

• You'll inherit a real, established estate with legacy telemetry gaps to close, genuinely underexplored surface area, not a well-mined problem.

About Birdeye
Birdeye is the leading agentic marketing platform for multi-location brands. Companies like H&R Block, Aspen Dental, and Caesars Entertainment use Birdeye to manage marketing across thousands of locations — from how they get found, to how they convert, to how they retain customers. Our platform replaces disconnected point tools with AI agents that execute work at the location level — responding to reviews, updating listings, publishing content, and driving conversions.

Backed by Marc Benioff, Jerry Yang, and Accel-KKR, Birdeye was named to G2’s 2026 Best Agentic AI Products list — appearing alongside the world’s leading AI companies. We’re expanding rapidly into enterprise, with growing adoption across large, multi-location brands.

The Opportunity
This is a hybrid role that combines data engineering, analytics, and product strategy. You'll build scalable datasets, design data pipelines, analyze massive amounts of search performance data, and partner with Product, Engineering, and Growth teams to identify what improves SEO and Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) performance across our platform. Rather than building customer-facing features, you'll build the intelligence that helps us decide what features to build next.

Your work will directly influence our product roadmap by helping answer questions like:
• What product capabilities have the greatest impact on organic visibility?
• Why are certain customers or industries outperforming others?
• How do search engine and AI search algorithm changes affect our customers?
• Which product investments create measurable improvements in rankings, traffic, and conversions?
• Where are our biggest opportunities to improve customer outcomes

What You'll Do
Build the Data Foundation
• Design, build, and maintain scalable data pipelines using SQL, Python, Snowflake, dbt, and modern data engineering practices
• Integrate and model data from Google Search Console, Google Business Profile, analytics platforms, ranking providers, AI visibility datasets, and internal product systems
• Ensure data quality, reliability, governance, and auditability across analytical datasets
• Develop reusable data models that support experimentation, reporting, and long-term product analytics
• Continuously improve the performance and scalability of our analytical data infrastructure

Discover What Drives Organic Performance
• Analyze billions of data points to identify the factors that influence SEO and AEO performance
• Investigate underperforming customers, industries, and locations to determine root causes
• Measure the impact of product features on rankings, visibility, traffic, engagement, and conversions
• Evaluate search engine and AI search algorithm updates across customer cohorts
• Build statistical analyses and experiments that separate correlation from causation
• Identify patterns and opportunities that inform future product investments

Turn Data into Product Strategy
• Build executive dashboards and self-service reporting using modern business intelligence and data visualization platforms
• Develop KPIs and measurement frameworks that quantify product impact
• Present clear, actionable recommendations to Product, Engineering, Growth, and executive leadership
• Partner with Product Managers to prioritize roadmap investments based on measurable customer outcomes
• Translate complex analytical findings into recommendations that improve customer visibility and product performance

Collaborate Across the Business
• Serve as the primary analytical partner across Data Engineering, Product, Growth, Customer Success, and Engineering
• Help define how Birdeye measures success across SEO, AEO, and AI visibility
• Establish scalable methodologies for evaluating product effectiveness
• Champion a culture of experimentation and data-driven decision making

AI-Driven Analytics
We expect AI to be part of how you work—not just something you build for others. Successful candidates are comfortable leveraging modern AI tools throughout the analytics lifecycle to:
• Accelerate SQL, Python, and data engineering workflows
• Explore large and complex datasets more efficiently
• Generate hypotheses and rapidly validate findings
• Automate repetitive analysis, documentation, and reporting tasks
• Improve productivity while maintaining high standards for data quality and analytical rigor

You understand where AI adds value, where human judgment is essential, and how to combine both to deliver better insights faster.

Technical Skills
What We're Looking For
• Expert-level SQL with experience analyzing large-scale datasets
• Strong Python programming skills for analytics, automation, and data engineering
• Experience designing and maintaining ELT/ETL pipelines
• Experience working with Snowflake or other modern cloud data warehouses
• Experience with dbt or similar data transformation frameworks
• Experience building executive dashboards and self-service reporting using modern business intelligence platforms
• Strong understanding of data modeling, performance optimization, and analytical best practices

Analytical Skills
• Exceptional analytical and problem-solving abilities
• Experience working with very large datasets and uncovering meaningful patterns
• Strong statistical reasoning and hypothesis-driven analysis
• Experience designing measurement frameworks and evaluating experiments
• Ability to distinguish correlation from causation and communicate findings with confidence
• Excellent communication skills with the ability to translate technical analysis into business recommendations

Domain Knowledge
Experience in one or more of the following areas is preferred:
• SEO and technical SEO
• Local search and Google Business Profile
• Multi-location business analytics
• Digital marketing analytics
• Answer Engine Optimization (AEO)
• AI search platforms and search visibility

28c0660f9f1c7f3e.description:
Headquarters: Remote
 
URL: http://onthegosystems.com

At OnTheGoSystems, the company behind WPML, Toolset, and PTC, we’re looking for a hands-on, AI-native marketer who wants to take ownership of marketing and help shape how we do it.

AI is a core part of how we work. We’re looking for someone who already uses AI agents, automation, integrations, and structured workflows to get real marketing work done – and can show us what they’ve achieved with them.

This is also a technical role. We’ve built our own analytics, newsletter, and marketing automation systems, so you should be comfortable working with technical tools, setting up a local development environment, and using tools like Claude to help you navigate technical tasks.

You won’t be joining an established marketing team or following a fixed playbook. You’ll have the freedom to talk to our clients, understand our business, find the strongest opportunities, and decide what marketing should focus on next.

What You’ll Work On

Several areas currently need an owner:

• 

SEO / GEO / AEO

• 

Content and collaborations with partners, authors, and bloggers

• 

Marketing to existing customers, including retention and expansion

• 

Paid advertising

• 

Client analytics

• 

Other marketing opportunities you identify

You’ll work hands-on, from identifying an opportunity through execution, measurement, and improvement.

Your First Weeks

We don’t expect you to arrive with all the answers. We want you to understand the business first and then decide what should be done.

You’ll:

• 

Learn our products, industry, competitors, and ecosystem.

• 

Speak directly with customers to understand their needs and how they see our products.

• 

Look at our data, existing activities, and opportunities.

• 

Identify where marketing can have the biggest impact.

• 

Build a concrete plan for the areas you propose to own and explain why.

What We’re Looking For

• 

You already use AI agents, automation, and advanced AI workflows in your everyday work and can show us concrete results.

• 

You’re hands-on and comfortable with the technical side of marketing.

• 

You’re curious and take time to understand customers and the business before proposing solutions.

• 

You can work across different areas of marketing and turn ideas into action.

• 

You understand how marketing connects to business results.

• 

You have experience marketing technical products, ideally software, SaaS, WordPress, or similar.

• 

You work independently and can move things forward without detailed instructions.

• 

You’re comfortable working in an environment where priorities can change and not everything is defined in advance.

Why Join Us

OnTheGoSystems is a profitable, self-funded product company growing since 2007. WPML powers more than 1.5 million websites worldwide.

You’ll have real ownership and the freedom to help build our marketing approach, work directly with our CEO and product teams, experiment with AI, and turn your ideas into real marketing initiatives.

We care about the people we work with and want to support them beyond their day-to-day work. Along with the flexibility of working remotely, we offer perks and benefits that support both work and life.

If you’re excited about building marketing with AI, getting hands-on, and having the freedom to shape what comes next, we’d love to hear from you.

To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/onthegosystems-head-of-marketing-1
